items.title: DHS Final Rule: Fixed Time Period of Admission & Extension of Stay (ends Duration of Status) for F, J, I nonimmigrants
items.summary: DHS published a final rule (doc. 2026-14439) on Jul 17, 2026, ending open-ended Duration of Status for F-1 students, effective Sep 15, 2026. Students get a fixed 'Admit Until Date' capped at 4 years (24 months for language programs); anyone needing more time must file Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) with USCIS in addition to the existing DSO SEVIS extension -- the I-539 EOS filing fee is reported as $420 filed online / $470 by paper. A timely-filed EOS gives up to 240 days of authorized stay while pending. The rule also shortens the F-1 post-completion grace period from 60 to 30 days for anyone who travels/re-enters or gets an EOS approval after the effective date. Students already in D/S status who remain continuously in the U.S. without leaving/re-entering keep transition protections, but only up to a hard outside cap of Nov 14, 2030 (4 years + 60-day grace period measured from the Sep 15, 2026 effective date).
items.notes: No lawsuit had been filed and no Congressional Review Act disapproval resolution had passed as of this run (checked 2026-08-14); coverage still describes litigation/CRA action as 'possible' or 'expected,' not filed. NAFSA remains publicly opposed. SEVP stakeholder webinar on the rule remains reported for Mon, Aug 31, 2026, 2-3pm ET, no advance registration, capped at 1,000 participants, recording to be posted after. Newly noted today: the Department of State's BridgeUSA program reportedly issued Guidance Directive 2026-01 on Aug 10, 2026 instructing J-1 sponsors on DS-2019/SEVIS record-keeping under this same final rule -- a J-1-specific parallel action, not independently confirmed against state.gov today, included here only as evidence that federal implementation activity is actively underway ahead of the Sep 15 effective date. IMPORTANT OPERATIONAL NOTE: the WebFetch tool failed for every domain attempted today, including non-government test domains (forbes.com, mondaq.com, en.wikipedia.org), not just the usual .gov targets -- a broader outage than prior runs' government-only egress blocks. All of today's findings therefore rely entirely on WebSearch result snippets/synthesis; no document could be directly rendered for verification today. Will retry direct .gov rendering each run.

items.title: USCIS Policy Alert PA-2026-05: officers may deny incomplete filings without issuing an RFE/NOID first
items.summary: Effective Aug 5, 2026, USCIS updated Policy Manual guidance so adjudicators may, at their discretion, deny a benefit request lacking required initial evidence or failing to establish eligibility without first issuing an RFE or NOID, and may set RFE response deadlines shorter than the prior 12-week norm (the 14-day international-mail grace period was also eliminated). Directly relevant to F-1 students filing Form I-539 (Extension of Stay) or I-765 under the new fixed-admission-period regime: an incomplete EOS package can now be denied outright with no chance to cure.
items.notes: Could not reach uscis.gov/policy-manual directly again this run -- today the WebFetch tool failed for every domain attempted, government and non-government alike (broader than the usual proxy-level .gov-only block seen on prior runs), so verification relied entirely on WebSearch snippets. Ten-plus independent law-firm/press sources continue to corroborate the exact Aug 5, 2026 effective date and mechanism with no contradicting reports, which is stronger-than-average secondary corroboration, but per the tracker's rule this stays 'Reported, unconfirmed' until an actual .gov page/PDF is rendered. Will keep retrying uscis.gov each run to move this to Confirmed.

items.title: DHS regulatory review of OPT / STEM OPT (RIN 1653-AA97) — no NPRM published yet
items.summary: DHS confirmed in a Jan 9, 2026 letter it is re-evaluating the scope and duration of OPT and STEM OPT, with a rulemaking entry (RIN 1653-AA97, titled 'Practical Training') in the Spring 2026 Unified Regulatory Agenda covering worker protection, fraud prevention, national security, and SEVP oversight goals. As of this run, no Notice of Proposed Rulemaking has been published in the Federal Register. A single secondary source (americanbazaaronline.com, Aug 11, 2026) reports the government's own unified agenda lists an NPRM target of February 2027 for this rule. OPT and STEM OPT remain fully operational and unchanged today. Relevant because many students planning an extra semester are also relying on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT timing.
items.notes: Could not reach reginfo.gov or federalregister.gov directly this run (WebFetch failed tool-wide today, not just for these domains) to confirm the RIN 1653-AA97 unified-agenda entry text or the reported Feb 2027 NPRM target. No OPT/STEM OPT NPRM exists yet to cite as of 2026-08-14. Will keep watching for actual NPRM publication.

items.title: Reported $100,000 fee under consideration for OPT / post-completion work authorization
items.source: Press reporting (Forbes, Bloomberg, ICEF Monitor, The PIE News, Higher Ed Dive)
items.summary: Multiple outlets report the administration is weighing a $100,000 fee applicable to OPT employment authorization (and by extension STEM OPT), modeled on the now-struck-down $100,000 H-1B fee proclamation. As of this run, no signed proclamation or DHS proposed rule/fee schedule has been reported for an OPT fee -- unlike the H-1B fee, which was signed via proclamation on Sep 19, 2025 and then struck down by a federal judge on Jun 8, 2026. Immigration attorneys quoted say an OPT fee is unlikely to survive legal challenge absent Congressional authorization, citing that H-1B precedent plus a Jul 24, 2026 appellate rejection of the administration's appeal. Who would pay (student/university/employer) remains unresolved. Directly relevant to students weighing an extra semester who are also counting on post-completion OPT/STEM OPT to work in the U.S. afterward.
items.notes: Still no DHS/USCIS/.gov statement, proposed rule, or signed proclamation found confirming or denying this as of 2026-08-14. Could not reach dhs.gov or uscis.gov newsroom directly this run (WebFetch failed tool-wide today). Related to but distinct from the RIN 1653-AA97 OPT/STEM OPT rulemaking review above -- reporting does not tie this fee proposal to that specific rulemaking docket.

items.title: NAFSA/JB International report: fall 2026 international enrollment projected to fall ~9.5% (~111,000 students) amid visa crackdown
items.source: NAFSA: Association of International Educators / JB International (research report, press reporting)
items.summary: A report released Aug 11, 2026 by NAFSA and research firm JB International, based on institutional responses to IIE's Spring 2026 Snapshot survey, projects fall 2026 international enrollment at U.S. colleges will fall about 9.5% (~111,000 fewer students), citing declining applications, visa-appointment bottlenecks, and newly restrictive immigration policy (including the D/S final rule) as converging headwinds. Estimated economic impact: ~$3.4 billion in lost local spending and ~39,000-40,000 jobs. Supporting data point noted today: Common App reports international submissions down ~9% for the 2026-27 cycle (India -14%, Ghana -34%, Nigeria -17%), with consulates in India, China, and across Europe reporting limited/delayed appointment availability. This is a research/economic-impact projection rather than a new rule -- it is being tracked here as evidence of how seriously the sector expects the policy changes above to bite, which is relevant context (not itself an actionable status change) for a student weighing an extra semester.
items.notes: This is a private-association economic/enrollment projection, not a government policy claim, so there is no .gov document that would ever 'confirm' it in the same sense as the other items -- it is tracked as 'Reported, unconfirmed' per the tracker's default schema, but readers should treat that label as 'not a government-verifiable fact' rather than 'possibly false.' Could not reach nafsa.org directly this run (WebFetch failed tool-wide today) to see if NAFSA has posted the underlying report/PDF itself.
